text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Deep vein thrombosis in the right leg 5 years prior. No other significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works as an accountant.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, recent injuries, heart disease, or diabetes. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is very unusual, as Pyelonephritis is an infection of the kidney and would not present as a chronic wound on the leg. Since you deny diabetes, I need to rule out venous insufficiency or arterial issues; does the wound improve when you elevate your leg, or does it hurt more when you walk? Also, does the skin around the wound feel hot or swollen, and do you notice any red streaks leading upward? REQUEST TEST: Venous Duplex Ultrasound; REQUEST TEST: Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Venous Duplex Ultrasound: Evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg; Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI): NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; the venous reflux explains the chronic nature of your leg wound, while the normal ABI rules out arterial insufficiency. To confirm the specific venous stasis etiology and assess for any underlying malignancy or specific infection, I need to see the wound. REQUEST IMAGES: Right lower leg wound and surrounding skin. While you prepare that, do you notice any varicose veins or a feeling of heaviness in that leg during the day?
